pr_title: Add AddedAffinity to NodeAffinity Filter and Score plugin
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind feature

/kind api-change

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

/sig scheduling

Add the AddedAffinity to the NodeAffinityArgs and use it in Filter and Score.

This can be used to replace legacy NodeLabel plugin with a more rich API that is consistent with PodSpec.
It can be useful to associate a scheduling profile with a set of Nodes.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #95738

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NodeAffinity plugin can be configured with AddedAffinity.
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

```docs
- [Usage]: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/scheduling/config/
- [KEP]: https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-scheduling/785-scheduler-component-config-api
```

issue_context.title: Add default node affinity constraints to NodeAffinity plugin
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:

/sig-scheduling

Configurable node affinity constraints to the NodeAffinity plugin args:

```golang
type NodeAffinityArgs struct {
  default *v1.NodeAffinity
}
```

These rules are always appended to the ones defined in PodSpecs.

**Why is this needed**:

Some scheduling profiles might only make sense for certain set of Nodes. Requiring PodSpecs to have node affinity additionally to the scheduler name is redundant in this scenario.
While this can be achieved with mutating webhooks, such implementation would increase Pod creation latency.

@Huang-Wei @ahg-g wdyt?
/sig scheduling

+1, I think this will allow us to give users a direct replacement to the custom `NodeLabel` plugin.

To clarify, the idea here is to merge, and so the "default" will always be applied to the spec irrespective of whether or not the pod defines one (so it is different from default podtopologyspread which we apply only if the pod spec doesn't define one).

LGTM. One question: if `NodeAffinityArgs` contains **hard** constraints, I think we should honor it in PodTopologySpread? (which now honors **explicit hard** node selector/affinity constraints from pod spec.)

> To clarify, the idea here is to merge, and so the "default" will always be applied to the spec irrespective of whether or not the pod defines one (so it is different from default podtopologyspread which we apply only if the pod spec doesn't define one).

I think so - they're ANDed, but leave to @alculquicondor to confirm.

The easy question first:
Yes, append == merge == AND

> if NodeAffinityArgs contains hard constraints, I think we should honor it in PodTopologySpread?

That should actually be the majority of use cases. What do you think of sharing the PreFilter state from NodeAffinity to PodTopologySpread to pass the calculated affinity?

> That should actually be the majority of use cases. What do you think of sharing the PreFilter state from NodeAffinity to PodTopologySpread to pass the calculated affinity?

I assume it wouldn't impose too much overhead on perf, right? BTW: we can make a minor improvement in PreFilter() for non-empty `metadata.name` (case of DasemonSet) - in which case, do an early return once we find a match.

> I assume it wouldn't impose too much overhead on perf, right?

The alternative would be for users of profiles to provide a webhook, which would be worst for the system, but cause the same overhead in scheduler.

> BTW: we can make a minor improvement in PreFilter() for non-empty metadata.name (case of DasemonSet)

I guess in this case we should skip applying the extra node selectors.
But we have a semantics problem if a DaemonSet Pod template has a scheduler name with hard node affinity rules. Then the daemonset controller would create unschedulable Pods, as it wouldn't consider the profile node affinity.

> in which case, do an early return once we find a match.

I'm not sure I follow. PreFilter is independent of Node.

> > in which case, do an early return once we find a match.
> 
> I'm not sure I follow. PreFilter is independent of Node.

Oh, you were just suggesting to pre-process the affinity spec in PreFilter(), instead of iterating over nodes to get a PreFilter result? If so, please ignore my comment about the overhead thing.




> > BTW: we can make a minor improvement in PreFilter() for non-empty metadata.name (case of DasemonSet)
> 
> I guess in this case we should skip applying the extra node selectors.
> But we have a semantics problem if a DaemonSet Pod template has a scheduler name with hard node affinity rules. Then the daemonset controller would create unschedulable Pods, as it wouldn't consider the profile node affinity.

I think we need to ensure DaemonSet controller to honor the profile's hard node affinity args, otherwise the DaemonSet's stauts will end up with X/Y available (X < Y, Y is the number of nodes which passed podTemplate's node affinity).

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5d49a6253c84c7f99264f0f95453ec666c998359/pkg/controller/daemon/daemon_controller.go#L891-L901

> Oh, you were just suggesting to pre-process the affinity spec in PreFilter()

Correct.

> I think we need to ensure DaemonSet controller to honor the profile's hard node affinity args.

That would imply that we have to make the daemonset controller profile aware, which, other than being a lot of work (it doesn't currently run a framework), it's prone to be misconfigured by operators.

Would it make sense to exclude DaemonSet Pods from this feature of default affinity rules?

> Would it make sense to exclude DaemonSet Pods from this feature of default affinity rules?

In that case, it seems on the scheduler side, the only clue is to tell if `.spec.metadata.name` is nil (checking a Pod's controllerRef is too much IMO)? It's for sure doable, but it's a bit fragile as `.spec.metadata.name` may be used for general purposes (not just reserved for DaemonSet) in the future.

> Would it make sense to exclude DaemonSet Pods from this feature of default affinity rules?

I don't think so, we should just document it.

Note that this is the same problem with NodeLabel plugin that already exists.

> Note that this is the same problem with NodeLabel plugin that already exists.

Do we have consensus? I would like to add this for 1.20
I am ok with this, it is a replacement to the NodeLabel plugin which we want to deprecate in this cycle.

> Do we have consensus?

Are we agreed on "exclude DaemonSet Pods from this feature of default affinity rules" by telling "if `.spec.metadata.name` is nil"?

I'm not sure what you mean by `.spec.metadata.name` being nil. Whose? The Pod?

Unless you mean the node affinity using `metadata.name` that Daemonset pods get:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/daemonset/#scheduled-by-default-scheduler

@ahg-g stance is to not do anything special with Daemonset Pods

I'm in the fence. Are there any other kind of Pods that could get affected?
The most reliable way to tell Daemonset Pods is via the controller reference IMO. But is it worth? There are other ways a user could get unschedulable Pods. We would need to make sure we are surfacing the error properly so that the user can fix their PodSpec by using a different scheduler or setting NodeAffinity themselves.

> > Do we have consensus?
> 
> Are we agreed on "exclude DaemonSet Pods from this feature of default affinity rules" by telling "if `.spec.metadata.name` is nil"?

I don't think we should do anything special for daemonsets, we just need to document the behaviour and propose a best practice. As I mentioned, this is not new, the existing nodelabel plugin has the same behavior.

> I don't think we should do anything special for daemonsets, we just need to document the behaviour and propose a best practice. As I mentioned, this is not new, the existing nodelabel plugin has the same behavior.

To clarify: in a cluster admin's angle, they should understand that a non-nil `NodeAffinityArgs` may cause a DaemonSet to create extra Pods in pending (unschedulable and unresolvable) state as profile-level node affinity constraints are not honored at Pod creation time (by DaemonSet controller).

> To clarify: in a cluster admin's angle, they should understand that a non-nil NodeAffinityArgs may cause a DaemonSet to create extra Pods in pending (unschedulable and unresolvable) state as profile-level node affinity constraints are not honored at Pod creation time (by DaemonSet controller).

The best practice would be to always have a default profile that doesn't set NodeAffinityArgs that daemonsets should use. If a second profile is added that explicitly targets a specific set of nodes, then daemonsets that use this profile being deployed only on those nodes is I think working as intended.

> The best practice would be to always have a default profile that doesn't set NodeAffinityArgs that daemonsets should use. If a second profile is added that explicitly targets a specific set of nodes, then daemonsets that use this profile being deployed only on those nodes is I think working as intended.

LGTM, we should ensure end-user / cluster admin to be aware of this.
/assign

review_comments: add a TODO to validate RequiredDuringSchedulingRequiredDuringExecution once implemented

Nit: is it more efficient to do a "smart merge" on addedAffinity and user-specified ones? so that we only run "match logic" once. For example, "foo in [bar]" and  "foo in [bar]" gets de-duplicated to "foo in [bar]"; while "foo in [bar]" and  "foo in [baz]" gets merged to one entry: "foo in [bar, baz]".

I don't think it's worth.
See my documentation PR https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/24914/files#diff-ba98b126fe5dd6bf0570b39d4928eb9143d1f2ed60fbaf9fa2051810acc2e8a6R192
Is this PR still a work in progress? can you please add WIP in the PR title if so?
It's not. Such API doesn't exist yet and no one is working on it, AFAIK.

If the pod specified a same prefered affinity with default one, then that will be double count. For example, the default one is 'in zoneA with weight=1', the pod specified one is 'in zoneA with weight=1 and in zoneB with wieght=2'. In the end, actually zoneA and zoneB have the same weight. That changed the original intent for the user. But this is indeed the `AND` behavior as the design, just thinking about whether this makes sense for the user. Although I see the major use-case for this feature is required affinity, so I may over thing about this.

You are correct, and I think that is working as intended.

However, in "AddedAffinity", you would probably use a label that Pods usually don't care about. I'll try to put some thoughts in kubernetes/website#24914

You updated the function name in this comment, but didn't actually change the function name. Also, wondering if we actually need this private function since it's just a wrapper for `corev1.MatchNodeSelectorTerms`
it can be removed when the TODO is implemented.
